features.label: Stochastic same sample two point convex pseudo regret

context.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.

object.definition: Samples $\xi_t$ are i.i.d. Each sample function $F(\cdot;\xi)$ is almost surely convex on $\mathbb R^d$, with a global random Lipschitz constant $G(\xi)$ satisfying $\mathbb E G(\xi)^2\le L^2$. The population function $f(x)=\mathbb E F(x;\xi)$ is finite. Centers lie in $B_2^d(R)$; both probes may lie anywhere in $\mathbb R^d$.

assumption.description: For almost every xi under P, F(·;xi) is convex on all of R^d.

source_value: Root-mean-square sample Lipschitz bound; sample distribution and realizations are hidden.

bindings.source_value: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.

The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.
Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.
The native target is $\inf_{\mathcal A}\sup_{(F,P)}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A,\xi_{1:T}}[R_T]$.

Choose one algorithm using public inputs before taking the worst case over all admissible instances. Expectation covers the algorithm's private randomness and the observation randomness specified by the model. Comparator choice and the order of summation, minimization, and expectation follow the displayed formula.

comparators.definition: The minimizer of the population objective $f$ on the ball, without taking a hindsight minimum over sample realizations.

domains.definition: The center domain incurring objective loss is the Euclidean ball $B_2^d(R)$.

norms.definition: Euclidean two-norm on the explicitly specified d-dimensional function argument, gradient, or model vector.

objects.definition: Samples $\xi_t$ are i.i.d. Each sample function $F(\cdot;\xi)$ is almost surely convex on $\mathbb R^d$, with a global random Lipschitz constant $G(\xi)$ satisfying $\mathbb E G(\xi)^2\le L^2$. The population function $f(x)=\mathbb E F(x;\xi)$ is finite. Centers lie in $B_2^d(R)$; both probes may lie anywhere in $\mathbb R^d$.
The distribution P is fixed and unknown. Samples ξ_t are i.i.d. and independent of history and algorithmic randomness.
The population objective f(x)=E_xi F(x;xi) is finite on R^d; the second-moment Lipschitz assumption implies that the mean objective is Lipschitz.

protocols.adversary_information: Distributions or functions are fixed before interaction. A round’s fresh sample is drawn after the action and probes are chosen, independently of past history and the learner’s private randomness.
protocols.loss_bearing_points: Only the center x_t incurs sample-function loss; the two probes incur no additional loss. Expected loss equals f(x_t).
protocols.past_requery: The learner may not request new information from past rounds or previously used samples. Previously received feedback may be stored and processed. In stochastic models, an action may be repeated in a new round, using a fresh charged sample.
protocols.queries_per_round: Each round uses one fresh sample and two function values, totaling T samples and 2T scalar values.
steps: The function F and sample distribution are fixed. The parameters d, T, L, and R are public.
The history jointly determines center $x_t$ and probes $z_t^+,z_t^-$.
Draw ξ_t. The center incurs the current sample-function loss F(x_t;ξ_t).
Return both probe values from the same sample; the target is pseudo-regret for the population mean f.

variable_blocks.space: The space $\mathbb R^d$ is the global function's formal domain, distinct from the ball-constrained centers and actual probes.
